title: Pixelator
techniques: a background copy of the photo per block, sized and positioned so each block is a lens
one magnification from wide glass block (below 1) through clear (1) to a flat pixel (100,000)
column and row from sibling-index() with mod() and round()
registered numbers, shared ones worked out once on the wall and inherited
glass sheen and bevel as one patterned sheet over the wall, a block wide
frosted glass: one backdrop-filter blur on that sheet, sized from the block
press a block flat: the block under the pointer takes a magnification of 1 and eases back
columns and rows from sqrt() of the photo's aspect ratio
a small script keeps the block count in step and swaps in your own photo; the sliders are the Controls panel's

features.name: sibling-index()
features.baseline: newly available (2026-08-18); the script writes --i where it is missing, and without either the frame shows the plain photo

features.name: CSS round() and mod()
features.baseline: newly available (2024-05); plain photo without them

features.name: backdrop-filter
features.baseline: newly available (2024-09); without it the Frosted switch only milks the glass

inspiration.title: Michelangelo's David, Florence 2019 (the default photo, CC BY 2.0, resized)
inspiration.author: George M. Groutas

exceptions.script: scene.js works out the wall's columns and rows and keeps that many block elements in the page, swaps the photo for one the visitor picks in the Controls panel, drops or pastes, and writes --i where sibling-index() is missing. The lenses and the glass are CSS.
exceptions.rasterImage: assets/david.jpg (800x1200 JPEG, 94 KB) is the default photo, asked for by the founder on 2026-11-10. It loads as a separate file and is not part of the 14 KiB page budget.
